assumptions: no verification oracle: the server never observes accept/reject outcomes

dataseal_original.authentication: DataSeal checksum rows; fixed key fixture K=rnd(seed 3), alpha=7
dataseal_original.evaluation_keys: rotation keys only (no relinearisation, no row swap)
dataseal_original.forgery_bound: no bound claimed (attack target in Experiment A)
dataseal_original.packing: controlled: stride n+2 (tiled: 66); native: stride n (DataSeal n+2; tiled 64/66); n=128 tiled T=64 (cmd/finaleval rule)

basis: Lattigo preset: bfv.DefaultParams (incl. PN14QP438) documented as 'ensuring 128 bit security in the classic setting' (lattigo v2.2.1-0.20210923173451 bfv/params.go:92-93)

HomomorphicEncryption.org security standard (Albrecht et al., 2018), classical 128-bit table: N=2^14 allows log2(QP) <= 438 for a uniform ternary secret with sigma ~ 3.2; PN14QP438 has logQP = 438 (at the bound, includes the key-switching modulus P)
secret distribution: rlwe GenSecretKey = ternary with P(0)=P(+1)=P(-1)=1/3 (rlwe/keygen.go:61-62, ring/ring_sampler_ternary.go:20-23); error sigma = 3.2 (rlwe/params.go:27)
the plaintext modulus t does not enter the RLWE hardness estimate, so the PN14QP438-T54 profile (only T changed) keeps the same basis
he_security.estimator: lattice-estimator not run (not available offline in this environment); the claim rests on the standard table and the Lattigo preset documentation
